cloze.title: Say it the exam way
cloze.text:
Light from a galaxy moving away from us is shifted to [[longer|shorter]] wavelengths. This is called [[redshift|blueshift]]. The redshift of a galaxy is the change in wavelength divided by the [[rest|observed]] wavelength. Redshift has [[no unit|the unit m]].

For a slowly moving galaxy, redshift is the ratio of its recessional velocity to the [[speed of light|speed of sound]]. More distant galaxies are moving away [[faster|slower]]. The Hubble–Lemaître law links recessional velocity and [[distance|wavelength]]. It lets us estimate the [[age|mass]] of the Universe.

warmup_p2.alt: State the name of the law that allows the age of the Universe to be estimated. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2026 Paper 2 Question 3(c), 1 mark: Hubble-Lemaître (Law). Also accepted: Hubble's (Law). Not accepted: Hubble's constant.

mc.alt: The redshift of a distant galaxy is 0.014. According to Hubble's law, the distance of the galaxy from Earth is: A 9.66 × 10⁻¹² m, B 1.83 × 10²⁴ m, C 1.30 × 10²⁶ m, D 9.32 × 10²⁷ m, E 6.33 × 10³⁹ m.
fb: Not this one. This multiplies <var>v</var> by <var>H</var><sub>0</sub>. Rearrange <var>v</var> = <var>H</var><sub>0</sub><var>d</var> to get <var>d</var> = <var>v</var> ÷ <var>H</var><sub>0</sub>.
Right. First the speed: v = zc = 0.014 × 3.00 × 108 = 4.2 × 106 m s−1. Then d = v ÷ H0 = 4.2 × 106 ÷ 2.3 × 10−18 = 1.83 × 1024 m.
Not this one. This divides <var>c</var> by <var>H</var><sub>0</sub>. The galaxy is not moving at the speed of light. Find its speed first: <var>v</var> = <var>z</var><var>c</var>.
Not this one. This divides <var>c</var> by <var>z</var>. Redshift is <var>z</var> = <var>v</var> ÷ <var>c</var>, so <var>v</var> = <var>z</var><var>c</var>, a multiply.
Not this one. This is far too large. Find <var>v</var> = <var>z</var><var>c</var> first, then divide by <var>H</var><sub>0</sub> once.

paper2.alt: Some galaxies have a very bright object at their centre called a quasar. A graph shows energy emitted per unit area per second against wavelength from 400 to 800 nanometres for a distant quasar, with peaks labelled H delta, H gamma, H beta and H alpha. (a)(i) The H gamma peak is observed at 503 nanometres; in a laboratory it is at 434 nanometres. Show that the redshift is 0.159. 2 marks. (a)(ii) Calculate the approximate distance from Earth to this quasar. 5 marks. (b) A second hydrogen line has a laboratory wavelength of 486 nanometres. Determine which peak on the graph this line corresponds to. Justify your answer by calculation. 3 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2026 Paper 2 Question 3(a)(b). (a)(i) 2 marks: z = (503 − 434) ÷ 434, z = 0.159. (a)(ii) 5 marks: z = v ÷ c, 0.159 = v ÷ 3.00 × 10⁸, v = H₀d, 0.159 × 3.00 × 10⁸ = 2.3 × 10⁻¹⁸ × d, d = 2.1 × 10²⁵ m. (b) 3 marks, justify by calculation: 0.159 = (λobserved − 486 × 10⁻⁹) ÷ 486 × 10⁻⁹, λobserved = 563 × 10⁻⁹ m, H beta. Look for H beta first, otherwise 0 marks.

paper2.alt: (C) A distant galaxy has a recessional velocity of 4.52 × 10⁶ metres per second. The hydrogen emission spectrum from the distant galaxy is viewed on Earth. Determine the observed wavelength of the same spectral line as in (c)(ii)(B), when viewed on Earth. 5 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2023 Paper 2 Question 10(c)(ii)(C), 5 marks: z = v ÷ c and z = (λobserved − λrest) ÷ λrest, 4.52 × 10⁶ ÷ 3.00 × 10⁸ = (λobserved − 486 × 10⁻⁹) ÷ 486 × 10⁻⁹, λobserved = 4.93 × 10⁻⁷ m, or consistent with (c)(ii)(B).

paper2.lead: Part (B) of this question found the line at 486 nm.

paper2.alt: Spectrum P is part of the hydrogen emission spectrum from a laboratory source. Spectrum Q shows the same lines from a distant galaxy, shifted towards increasing wavelength. (a)(i) Explain why the lines on spectrum Q are in a different position to those on spectrum P. 2 marks. (a)(ii) One line in spectrum P has a wavelength of 656 nanometres; the same line in spectrum Q is at 676 nanometres. Determine the recessional velocity of the galaxy. 5 marks. (b) The recessional velocity of another distant galaxy is 1.2 × 10⁷ metres per second. Calculate the approximate distance to this galaxy. 3 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for Specimen Paper 2 Question 5(a)(b). (a)(i) 2 marks: the galaxy is moving away from Earth (1); the apparent wavelengths of the lines have increased, or the light shows redshift (1). (a)(ii) 5 marks: z = (676 − 656) ÷ 656, v = z c, v = 9.15 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. (b) 3 marks: v = H₀d, 1.2 × 10⁷ = 2.3 × 10⁻¹⁸ × d, d = 5.2 × 10²⁴ m.

paper2.alt: Hubble's Law states that the universe is expanding. (b) A student plots some of the original data from the 1929 paper by Edwin Hubble: recessional velocity in metres per second, 0 to 600 000, against distance, 0 to 40 × 10²¹ m, with a line added. The student's gradient gives a Hubble constant of 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁷ per second. Age of universe = 1 ÷ H₀. (i) Calculate the age of the universe, in years, using the student's value for the Hubble constant. 2 marks. (ii) The current estimate is 13.8 × 10⁹ years. (A) State why the value obtained in (b)(i) is different from the current estimate. 1 mark. (B) Suggest a change the student could make to their graph to obtain a value closer to the current estimate. 1 mark.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2018 Section 2 Question 5(b). (i) 2 marks: age = 1 ÷ 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁷ = 5.0 × 10¹⁶ s, age = 1.6 × 10⁹ years. (ii)(A) 1 mark: the student's value for H₀ is too large or not accurate enough, or an incorrect line of best fit, or new or more accurate data is now available, or not enough data at large distances. (ii)(B) 1 mark: draw the correct line of best fit, or use a larger sample or all of the 1929 data, or use current data.

paper2.alt: Light from the Sun is used to produce a visible spectrum with dark lines. (b) The position of a hydrogen line is shown for a distant galaxy, a nearby galaxy and the Sun, at increasing wavelength. (i) Explain why the position of the line is different in each of the spectra. 2 marks. (ii) Show that the redshift of the light from the distant galaxy is 0.098. 2 marks. (iii) Calculate the approximate distance to the distant galaxy. 5 marks.

mi.alt: Marking instructions for 2015 Section 2 Question 4(b). (i) 2 marks: light is redshifted (1), as the galaxies are moving away (1); or further galaxies have greater recessional velocity. Blueshift is wrong physics, 0 marks. (ii) 2 marks: z = (450 − 410) ÷ 410 = 0.098. (iii) 5 marks: z = v ÷ c, 0.098 = v ÷ 3.00 × 10⁸, v = H₀d, 2.94 × 10⁷ = 2.3 × 10⁻¹⁸ × d, d = 1.3 × 10²⁵ m.
